turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and why did he find out from his phone in the middle of a class instead of me hearing it from you?
I don't think this is productive.
"Productive." My son got a zero without anyone speaking to me first; that's what we're here about. Answer the question, Hale, or I'm walking down to the principal's office.
I'm going to go. I have a class in ten minutes.
You asked for this meeting, Hale, and I'm not leaving it. Take the zero off Owen's essay, or I'm in the principal's office before your class starts.
Email the principal if you want. I'm done here.

I won't email, Hale; I'll be standing in that office in five minutes. I'll tell the principal you entered a zero before calling me, against the school's own procedure 4.2, and then refused to say on what basis. You can still sit down and answer me.
